_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401910046.text: Washington have won both meetings this season, including 116-96 on Nov 23, and come in rested after not playing since Tuesday. Orlando are still without Paolo Banchero (high ankle sprain), Jonathan Isaac and Noah Penda, and Kevin Porter Jr. is still reconditioning after signing this week. Anthony Davis (25.6 points, 10.1 rebounds) is playing well despite the trade talk. The news angle leans slightly Washington.

401910047.text: Brooklyn lost 124-100 in Toronto on Friday, so this is the second night of a back-to-back. Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. has been sitting one game of each back-to-back, and Jordi Fernandez says minutes must be earned through effort. Charlotte are short in the backcourt themselves. The news angle leans slightly Charlotte at home.

401910048.text: Indiana arrive on a back-to-back after a 111-87 loss in Philadelphia, with season lows of 87 points and 5-of-37 from three. Rick Carlisle said he did not like how they competed. Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) remains out. Chicago have been off since Wednesday but miss their two leading scorers, Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson. Buddy Hield and Jalen Smith face Indiana, their former team. Rest and morale lean Chicago.

401910049.text: Milwaukee (2-18) were knocked out of the Cup in Detroit on Friday and play again on the second night of a back-to-back. Taylor Jenkins says the team 'stopped trusting' what worked earlier. Oklahoma City expect Aday Mara and Jaylin Williams back, though Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are still out long-term. Everything leans Oklahoma City.

401910050.text: Philadelphia played their stars to clinch East Group B on Friday and are now resting them: Joel Embiid (plantar fasciitis management) and LeBron James (back) are out, along with Jaylen Brown (hamstring). Dean Wade is questionable. Houston's Steven Adams is questionable (knee). A depleted 76ers side on a back-to-back leans clearly Houston.

401910054.text: Both teams are out of the Cup. Miami won at New York on Friday (Giannis Antetokounmpo had 22 points and a career-high 23 rebounds), while Cleveland have lost two straight and trade talk is starting. Evan Mobley (toe) is ramping up, but Kenny Atkinson gave no return date. The news angle leans slightly Miami unless Mobley returns.

401910051.text: The Lakers blew a 16-point halftime lead in San Antonio and are out of the Cup. Luka Doncic is 13-of-64 from three over his last five games and had a postgame run-in with a fan. Austin Reaves is back. Memphis won their Cup group and are on a three-game win streak, but they are still without Cameron Boozer and Jerami Grant. Momentum favours Memphis and the healthier roster favours the Lakers, so the news is roughly neutral.

401910052.text: San Antonio are getting healthier: De'Aaron Fox started and Dylan Harper returned on a minutes limit in Friday's comeback win over the Lakers, and Victor Wembanyama is not on the injury report. Boston have lost five of six, including an 87-86 loss to Atlanta with 26 turnovers. Mitchell Robinson (COVID-19) is a game-time call. The news leans San Antonio.

401910053.text: Phoenix are coming off what Devin Booker called 'a meltdown': a blown 21-point lead against Dallas that ended their Cup run. Utah (3-17) lost to Denver, and Will Hardy said 'we need to toughen up.' Jusuf Nurkic made his season debut, but Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. remain out. Phoenix may come in rattled, but the talent gap still leans Phoenix.

401910055.text: Detroit have kept winning without Cade Cunningham (knee tendinopathy, no timeline). J.B. Bickerstaff is preaching patience, so expect caution with him. Orlando play the second night of a back-to-back, still without Paolo Banchero, and Detroit beat them 104-86 on Tuesday. The news leans Detroit.

401910056.text: New York were knocked out as defending Cup champions on Friday, and Karl-Anthony Towns admitted the disappointment. OG Anunoby (calf) is out again, and Miles McBride and Jordan Clarkson are day-to-day. Atlanta have won five straight after edging Boston to win their group, though CJ McCollum is still out. Form and mood lean Atlanta, against the numbers' home lean.

401910057.text: Toronto beat Brooklyn behind 34 points from Scottie Barnes but missed the Cup knockouts on point differential. Kawhi Leonard and RJ Barrett are still out, and starter Ja'Kobe Walter left Friday's game with a quad contusion. Denver beat Utah with Jamal Murray scoring 36. The Nikola Jokic extension chatter is background noise. The news leans slightly Denver.

401910058.text: Portland blew out Golden State wire to wire to win their Cup group. Damian Lillard (calf tightness) is day-to-day, and Ja Morant is close to returning from his hamstring strain. New Orleans snapped a four-game skid at the Clippers, but Dejounte Murray's trade request and 'sabotage' posts hang over the locker room. The news leans Portland.

401910059.text: Both teams are reeling: the Clippers have lost six straight (4-14), and Golden State were routed in Portland and knocked out of the Cup. Stephen Curry (oblique) is ruled out for this game, and Bradley Beal sits for the Clippers. Neither side has a clear news edge, so the read is roughly neutral.

401910060.text: Sacramento (2-16) are being talked about as deadline sellers, with Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter the likeliest names, and LaVine (knee) has been out. Minnesota lost in Memphis and are still without Anthony Edwards. LaMelo Ball (ankle) is day-to-day, and this game is his likely return target. The news leans Minnesota.
